states.changed: A reader meets every sentence of the International AI Safety Report 2026 that speaks of evaluating AI systems, as a strip through the report and as squares by section, can colour them by what each rests on, what its test is for and whose evidence it cites, and reads that the report's evaluation evidence leans on industry and that no sentence names a public body as setter of a pass mark.

A reader now meets, behind the report's 41 measured sentences, the 58 sources they rest on as tiles sorted by whether anyone outside the maker could repeat the test and coloured by who ran it, the nine losses of control of step 3 beside the Atelier's coding, and reads that outsiders could repeat 27 of the 48 tests while every pass mark and every loss of control on record stays with the maker.

A reader now meets the check: every sentence, source and case read a second time, blind, with the agreement code by code; a funnel from the 48 tests behind the results to the 28 an outsider could repeat on paper, the 12 whose source holds the result the report cites in full and the one on open weights; each tile marked with whether its source holds the result; and three dated corrections, the largest that 27 of 48 checkable tests becomes 12 of 48 once each source is read for the result it is cited for.

A reader now meets the paper beside the page and a section read for it: every share drawn against all 201 sentences on evaluation (10, or 5 %, held in full by a test an outsider could repeat); the 16 tests on control as tiles, each repeatable one that holds its result marked with how the behaviour was brought about (trained, told or asked, never untold); the test sources grouped by organisation; and the seven public instruments the report names, coded twice, in a table whose every cell opens to its passage, showing that none sets a pass mark, three leave it to the developer and six name a loss of control.

A reader now meets, after the presentation, every one of the 28 tests an outsider could repeat as a row of the models it ran on, each coloured by what its maker's own page says today (retired, offered with a shutdown announced, offered), switchable to the page as presented; and a dated correction in the answer, the check and the paper: 23 of the 28 name a model since retired, not 6, and of the 12 results that hold, 2 can still be run on every model they name, 1 after 1 December.
